newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees public spending growth in H2.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees public spending growth in H2.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Tuesday that growth in the second half of 1996 would be spurred by a seasonal increase in public spending, though he insisted the budget would end the year in balance.

"In keeping with our objectives of a balanced budget for this year, the seasonality of public spending in the second half, equivalent to additional spending of around 1 point of (gross domestic) product in annualized terms, will allow this to be one more factor in promoting productive activity," Ortiz said in an address to Mexico's Congress.

Ortiz echoed President Ernesto Zedillo, who said Sunday Mexico aimed to achieve growth of at least 4 percent in 1997, adding that the government was not going to change its economic program to achieve that goal.

"The balance in public finances, a congruent monetary policy and the floating exchange rate regime, will continue being fundamental pillars of stability. That will allow the marked drop in inflation to continue and will encourage lower interest rates," Ortiz said.
Zedillo outlined the 4 percent growth target for 1997 in his State of the Nation address Sunday.
